ai.description: Hawksbill turtles reach 60–90 cm in length. They feature a patterned, overlapping scute carapace and a narrow, bird-like beak. The shell displays distinct brown and yellow mottled coloration.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Hawksbill is best identified by its narrow, bird-like beak and overlapping, serrated scutes on the carapace, which distinguish it from all other Indian sea turtles.
ai.habitat: Hawksbill turtles in the Indian subcontinent primarily inhabit tropical coral reefs and rocky areas, nesting on undisturbed sandy beaches backed by coastal vegetation.
ai.behavior: Hawksbill turtles are primarily diurnal, using their narrow, bird-like beaks to forage for sponges tucked deep within crevices of coral reefs.
ai.reproductionNotes: Hawksbill turtles are oviparous, nesting primarily from September to January in India. They lay clutches of 90–160 eggs on sandy beaches.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Hawksbill turtle occurs along India’s tropical coasts, primarily nesting in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, and sporadically along the mainland shores.
